top_story: Syria’s arrest on 24 April of Amjad Youssef, a central perpetrator of the 2013 Tadamon massacre, signals a rare move toward accountability for Assad-era atrocities and reflects a political effort to reframe state authority after years of impunity. The same day, Gaza’s social collapse showed a different but related pattern of civilian harm, with widespread trauma leaving many children unable to speak and the breakdown of civil order separating dozens from their families each week. Since Trump’s 23 March threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure unless Tehran reopens the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian warnings of regional escalation have sharpened the wider atmosphere of coercion and insecurity. The regional picture is one in which unresolved violence is no longer only a matter of front lines, but of institutions, families, and children absorbing its long aftershocks.
